Rightsizing rule: for each instance, required_vcpu = current_vcpu * p95_cpu_pct/100 / 0.7 and required_mem = current_memory_gib * p95_mem_pct/100 / 0.8. The recommended type is the cheapest instance_type in the SAME family (from instance_catalog.csv) with vcpu >= required_vcpu and memory_gib >= required_mem. An on-demand instance costs $0.192/hour. A 1-year partial-upfront Reserved Instance costs $1000 upfront plus $0.075/hour. Assuming the instance runs 730 hours per month, after how many months (fractional, 2 decimals) does the RI become cheaper than on-demand (break-even point)?

Same RI as before: $2150 all-upfront for 1 year versus $0.384/hour on-demand. What is the minimum utilization (percentage of the 8760 hours the instance must actually run) for the RI to be no more expensive than paying on-demand only for the hours used? Round to 2 decimals.

A Compute Savings Plan has a commitment of $10.0/hour and gives a 28% discount off on-demand. In each hour, eligible usage is first priced at the discounted rate and charged against the commitment (unused commitment is still paid); any discounted cost above the commitment is instead billed at full on-demand rates for the uncovered portion. Over 8 hours the on-demand cost of usage per hour was [12, 8, 15, 6, 10, 14, 9, 11] dollars. What is the total cost with the Savings Plan over these 8 hours, and the saving versus pure on-demand? Round to 2 decimals.
A 3-year partial-upfront RI costs $3600 upfront plus $0.05/hour for every hour of the term (8760 hours/year). What is its effective (amortized) hourly rate? Round to 4 decimals.
